0.0.n: Used to open the video cheerfully, rather than answer a question.

0.2.n: Adds a friendly, casual touch to the greeting こんにちは.

0.3.n: A standard daytime greeting that also works for addressing viewers.

0.6.n: A polite ending identifying the speaker; Japanese leaves out I here.

1.0.n: Combines with ことで to introduce the next topic.

1.1.n: Turns the preceding idea into a thing or situation within the transition ということで.

1.2.n: Completes ということで, linking the introduction to the main topic.

1.3.n: Refers to this video or presentation, not necessarily today.

1.4.n: Marks 今回 as the topic: what this installment will cover.

1.5.n: In 今回はですね, this adds politeness while the speaker pauses before continuing.

1.6.n: Softens the pause and keeps the audience engaged.

1.8.n: Politely points to the item being presented.

1.9.n: Links こちら to ございます as part of でございます, a very polite equivalent of です.

1.10.n: The connecting form of ござる; with で and ます, it creates a very polite statement.

1.11.n: Completes ございます and gives the presentation a formal, courteous tone.

2.0.n: This is the name of the technology company.

2.2.n: Adds a conversational pause without changing the relationship expressed by の.

2.4.n: 高 means high; コスパ abbreviates cost performance, expressing how much you get for the price.

2.5.n: Connects the description sub-brand to its name, POCO; it does not indicate ownership here.

2.7.n: Marks POCO as the source of the new phone.

2.8.n: Adds a polite pause after から while the sentence continues.

2.9.n: Keeps the explanation conversational and invites the listener’s attention.

3.0.n: The adverb form of 新しい, made by changing い to く, describes how the phone appeared.

3.1.n: 登場する becomes 登場しました in the polite past form, presenting the launch as completed.

4.0.n: Describes the phone as the newest available.

4.1.n: Connects 最新 to the following phone description, making it mean the latest phone.

4.2.n: Combines 高コスパ, good value for money, with ハイエンド, premium-tier, and スマホ, short for smartphone.

5.0.n: This is the brand name at the start of the phone’s full model name.

5.2.n: This letter is part of the model name, not a separate Japanese word.

5.3.n: This number is part of the phone’s model name.

5.5.n: This is a model-name label, not a description of a person’s profession.

5.7.n: This is another label within the phone’s model name.

5.9.n: An excited spelling of 来た, the plain past form of 来る; the long vowel emphasizes the celebration.

0.lit: Okay, hi there, hello, Suzu am.
0.tip: Japanese often omits I, so すずです naturally introduces the speaker as Suzu.

1.lit: That being so, as for this time, you see, this here it is.
1.tip: でございます is a very polite version of です, used here to present the item.

2.lit: Xiaomi’s, you see, high-value sub-brand, POCO, from, you see,
2.tip: から marks the brand the phone comes from; the sentence continues into the next line.

3.tip: ました marks a polite past statement: the phone has already appeared or launched.

4.tip: コスパ refers to value for money, not simply a low price.

5.tip: キター stretches 来た into an enthusiastic announcement, like It’s here!
